data.title: Anthropic shares slip after rallying in record-breaking IPO debut
data.description:
Anthropic shares fell in their second day of trading as a broader market selloff and growing concerns over the AI trade weighed on sentiment following the stock’s record-setting debut.

The company’s shares fell as much as 7.4% in early premarket trading Friday, a day after surging 17% in their public market debut. The stock traded as low as $90 as of 4:02 a.m. in New York, compared with Thursday's closing price of $97.17. Shares remained above the IPO price of $83.

The decline came amid broader market weakness, with Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.9%. The initial surge reflected strong investor demand for the heavily oversubscribed IPO, but the company's steep valuation and fresh competitive threats weighed on shares Friday as investors broadly pulled back from riskier assets.

Anthropic’s $107.3B IPO attracted global demand for seven times the shares on offer. Competition was so intense that more than half of institutional investors bidding for shares received no allocation, Bloomberg reported Thursday. The IPO surpassed the previous record set by SpaceX in June, which raised a total of $86.25B, including additional shares sold by underwriters through the overallotment option.

Goldman Sachs Group , Morgan Stanley , and 20 other banks earned a record $550M in fees for their work on Anthropic’s IPO.

data.title: Eimskipafélag Íslands hf. – Sale of a New Bond Series
data.description:
Eimskipafélag Íslands hf. has completed an auction for a new bond series, EIM 261130. Bids amounting to ISK 2,500 million were accepted at a yield of 8.50%. The bonds will be sold at par. A total of 17 bids amounting to ISK 2,700 million were received, with yields ranging from 8.20% to 8.75%. The bonds will be sold at par.

The bonds are non-indexed with a four-year maturity and quarterly interest payments, with the first interest payment on 26 February 2027. The principal will be repaid in full on the maturity date, 26 November 2030. The bonds are issued in denominations of ISK 20,000,000.

Payment and settlement are scheduled for Thursday, 26 November 2026. An application will be made for admission of the bond series to trading on the Nasdaq Iceland Main Market. Under the terms of the issue, the bonds shall be admitted to trading within six months of the issue date, i.e. no later than 26 May 2027.

Landsbankinn Corporate Finance and Capital Markets managed the auction and will arrange the admission of the bond series to trading on the Nasdaq Iceland Main Market.

In connection with the proposed admission of the bond series to trading, a prospectus will be published on the Company’s investor website, https://www.eimskip.com/investors, following approval by the Financial Supervisory Authority of the Central Bank of Iceland and before trading in the bonds commences.

For further information, please contact:

Guðbjörg Birna Björnsdóttir, Head of Treasury at Eimskip, tel. +354 844 4752 or investors@eimskip.com.

Gunnar S. Tryggvason, Fixed Income Sales at Landsbankinn, tel. +354 821 2090 or gunnars@landsbankinn.is.

This is Eimskip

Since 1914 Eimskip has been a trusted partner in global logistics with a network spanning 20 countries, 56 offices and 1,700 employees. To ensure reliable door-to-door solutions for our customers, our services include container and reefer vessel operations in the North-Atlantic, terminal operations, trucking systems, warehouses, cold storages and a global forwarding network.

data.title: India's RBI expected to raise rates in December, deliver final hike in February
data.description:
Key points:
  • RBI to raise repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% on December 4, say 56 of 61 economists
  • Majority expect final hike to 6% in February as inflation tops target

By Pranoy Krishna

The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to raise its key interest rate to 5.75% on December 4, followed by a final hike in February, a Reuters poll of economists showed, as inflation breaches the upper end of the central bank's 2%-6% target band.

An energy price shock triggered by the war in the Middle East, coupled with uneven and deficient monsoon rainfall, pushed inflation past the RBI's 6% threshold in October for the first time in two years.

Other major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, are also expected to raise rates in December to fight persistently high inflation.

With India's economic growth expected to remain strong, the RBI, which kick-started its rate-hiking cycle last month, has room to tighten policy further, analysts say.

More than 90% of economists, 56 of 61, in a November 13-20 Reuters poll forecast the RBI to hike its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% at the conclusion of its December 2-4 policy meeting.

While three economists expected the central bank to leave rates unchanged, two predicted a larger 50-basis-point increase.

A majority of economists, 34 of 46, also forecast the RBI to follow up with a final hike to 6% in February.

"The inflation outlook has deteriorated in the last few months ... the fact that India is growing much faster than we had expected — could be north of 8% easily — I think that gives the RBI more latitude to prioritise elevated inflation, which has now breached the upper end of the tolerance range," said Dhiraj Nim, senior economist at ANZ.

"There is a clear generalisation of pressures beyond transitory parts of CPI, which are energy and food."

Despite a recent decline in crude oil , prices are nearly 30% above prewar levels, suggesting inflation will remain elevated in the near term.

However, the rupee's turnaround from one of Asia's worst-performing currencies to one of its best-performing could give the RBI space to moderate the pace of tightening. The central bank has spent billions of dollars to defend the currency against the dollar this year.

Still, a cumulative 75-basis-point increase would mark the shallowest tightening cycle in more than eight years.

"The chatter around aggressive rate hikes was only building up because the rupee was under significant pressure just a month ago. At this point, they (RBI) will be a little more comfortable," said Upasna Bharadwaj, chief economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, who expects two more rate hikes.

Bharadwaj added inflation would remain elevated and closer to the 6% mark for the next five to six months.

While inflation was forecast to average 6% in the fourth quarter and come down in the subsequent quarters, it was expected to stay above the RBI's medium-term target of 4% this year and next — a view broadly unchanged from the October poll.

Elevated prices will weigh on household spending and slow economic activity over the coming quarters.

The economy likely grew about 8% on average over the past five quarters, including the one just ended, but is expected to slow to 6.9% this quarter and 6.8% next, the survey showed.

"Growth is improving purely because of government expenditure and, to a certain extent, because of urban consumption ... But (from) this quarter onwards, I don't think these two stories will play as much," said Debopam Chaudhuri, chief economist at Piramal Group.

(Other stories from the November Reuters global economic poll)

data.title: Global Bond Yields Fall as Investors Seek Safe-Haven Assets — Update
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru

Yields on U.S., U.K., and eurozone government bonds dropped on Friday as risk-off sentiment continued to drive demand to safe-haven assets.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.6 basis points to 4.996%, while the U.K. 10-year yield dropped 4.5 bps to 5.271%, according to Tradeweb. Ten-year German Bund yields declined 6.2 bps to 3.339%.

A record initial public offering by Anthropic, which raised $81 billion, failed to revive appetite for artificial-intelligence stocks. Investors continued to question whether the enormous investments in the AI industry would pay off given the rising public resistance toward the industry.

"The blockbuster debut [IPO] couldn't sweep those worries under the rug," Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said in a note.

Asian and European stocks sold off on Friday as sentiment continued to deteriorate even after some positive news in the tech industry this week.

"When neither a blockbuster Nvidia beat nor the largest IPO in history can lift the tape, market psychology has fundamentally flipped from dip-buying to structural de-risking," Patrick Munnelly, partner at Tickmill Group, said in a note.

High borrowing costs also raise concerns about AI companies' ability to continue raising funds to finance their massive expansion.

"The scale of the Democratic win in the midterm [elections] has deepened worry that policymakers could push for slower data-center spending," David Groman, global equity strategist at Citi, said in a note.

The concerns about the tech and AI sector are driving the flight to safety, causing government bond yields to drop, Groman said.

Write to Miriam Mukuru at miriam.mukuru@wsj.com

data.title: Japan Tobacco cuts dividend by a quarter after losing control in Russia
data.description:
Japanese cigarette maker Japan Tobacco has cut its 2026 dividend by a quarter after losing control of its Russian business, the company said on November 19.

The board cut the final payout to JPY68 ($0.43) a share from the JPY136 ($0.85) it had planned in July, bringing the full-year dividend to JPY204 ($1.28) against a forecast of JPY272 ($1.70), according to its revised forecast filed with the Tokyo Stock Exchange. The chairman, the vice-chairman and three representative directors will take a 50% cut in base pay for two months, and the representative directors will forgo their 2026 bonuses.

The dividend cut will also reduce income for the Japanese state, which owns about 37% of Japan Tobacco. The Finance Ministry received JPY156bn ($975mn) in dividends for the previous financial year, according to Reuters, as reported by IntelliNews. Japan Tobacco appears to be the first Japanese group caught by the Kremlin's temporary-management regime for foreign-owned assets.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi raised the protection of Japanese business interests with President Vladimir Putin when they met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on November 18, Bloomberg reported, citing Japan's foreign ministry. It was the first face-to-face meeting between the two countries' leaders in seven years. Tokyo has protested through diplomatic channels and called for the decision to be reversed.

Putin's decrees of November 5 and November 6 put all seven of the group's Russian subsidiaries under the temporary management of Moscow-based Industrial Assets. The first covered the factory companies Petro in St Petersburg and JTI Donskoy Tabak in Rostov-on-Don and the leaf processors JTI Yelets in the Lipetsk region and Cres Neva in the Leningrad region. The second added the sales company JTI Russia, the dormant Pereslavl-Tabak and J.T.I. Innovative Products, which sold Ploom heated-tobacco devices.

The regime leaves Japan Tobacco with legal title but stops it taking operating decisions, so under IFRS the group deconsolidated the seven companies with effect from November 6 and expects to book a loss of about JPY1.377 trillion ($8.6bn) on losing control. About JPY1.5 trillion ($9.4bn) of assets, including goodwill, and JPY200bn ($1.25bn) of liabilities leave its balance sheet, along with about JPY400bn ($2.5bn) in cash.

The deconsolidation does not mean giving up ownership, selling the business or leaving Russia, where the local companies are still trading, chief executive Takehiko Tsutsui and chief financial officer Hiromasa Furukawa told investors in a presentation on November 19. The company said it would take every possible step to protect its rights and assets.

Japan Tobacco now expects a 2026 operating loss of JPY368bn ($2.3bn) instead of a JPY1.041 trillion ($6.5bn) profit, and a net loss of JPY724bn ($4.5bn) where it had forecast a JPY662bn ($4.1bn) profit. It cut its revenue forecast to JPY3.84 trillion ($24bn) from JPY3.903 trillion ($24.4bn). Before the decrees, Russia was expected to provide about 10% of group revenue and 25% of adjusted operating profit this year.

The group will aim for a payout ratio of about 70% from 2027, at the bottom of its 75% plus or minus five points policy range, and expects adjusted operating profit at constant exchange rates to grow by more than 10% a year in 2027-29 on a basis that excludes Russia, with the dividend rising from JPY204.

Japan Tobacco has been in Russia since 1999, when it bought the international business of RJ Reynolds. Its brands there include Winston, Camel, LD, Sobranie and Mevius, and it estimated its share of the Russian cigarette market at 36.9% at the end of 2025, Forbes Russia reported.

data.title: Norway's overall oil, gas output higher than forecast in October
data.description:
Norway's combined oil and gas production exceeded an official forecast by 1.8% in October, the Norwegian Offshore Directorate (NOD) said on Friday.

Norway is Europe's largest supplier of natural gas and a major producer of oil, but output varies from month to month depending on maintenance needs and other stoppages at its 100 offshore fields.

Overall oil, condensate, natural gas liquids and gas output stood at 0.678 million standard cubic metres per day, equivalent to 4.26 million barrels of oil equivalent, an increase of 1% year-on-year.

data.title: U.S. stock futures mixed as Anthropic debut fails to revive AI trade
data.description:
U.S. stock futures were mixed early Friday as investors assessed the fallout from Wall Street's sharp selloff in the previous session, when major indexes tumbled more than 2% each.

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities.

Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.85% while S&P 500 futures slipped 0.33%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures edged up 0.05%.

Anthropic's historic Nasdaq debut on Thursday marked the first pure-play AI lab to go public. Shares opened at $111.50, 33% above the IPO price of $83, before retreating to close at $96.97. Despite the scale of the debut, the stock's retreat from its opening price failed to provide the broader AI trade with a sustained boost. ANT shares are down 6% premarket.

U.S. Treasury yields moved lower across the curve. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 4.1 basis points to 4.73%, while the 10-year Treasury yield dropped 3.8 basis points to 5.01%. The 30-year Treasury yield declined 3.1 basis points to 5.38%.

Investors will look to the final February reading of the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index for fresh signals on the economy. BJ's Wholesale is also scheduled to report quarterly results before the opening bell.

Top S&P 500 gainers included CBRE +8.32%, KKR +5.65%, and Aon +2.00%. Decliners included Ross Stores -4.74%, Solventum -4.32%, and West Pharmaceutical Services -2.44%.

data.title: British Bank Backed by Kushner's Affinity Gets U.S. License — WSJ
data.description:
By Margot Patrick

British business bank OakNorth, whose shareholders include Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners investment firm and the SoftBank Vision Fund, received a full-charter U.S. banking license that will let it increase an effort to lend more in the U.S.

OakNorth said it is the first foreign digital bank to be granted such a charter, which it received as part of its acquisition of a small bank in Michigan, Community Unity Bank.

The details

OakNorth applied in 2024 for the U.S. license and opened a representative office in New York. It agreed to acquire Community Unity in March 2025. Last year, around 40% of OakNorth's new lending was in the U.S.

With the U.S. license secured, it will now be able to take deposits and make loans directly through its U.S. bank, instead of via the U.K., and sign on customers in any state.

OakNorth Chief Executive Rishi Khosla said the lender wants to help entrepreneurs break out of the box of traditional banking by looking at where they are going in terms of financial prospects, not just where they have been. A typical customer might have $5 million to $100 million annual revenue, he said.

"That model of helping those underserved, proven entrepreneurs, which we focus on in the U.K., translates incredibly well to the U.S.," Khosla said in an interview. "You almost are pushing into an open door because a lot of these businesses, their alternative today is going to community banks." Khosla said those can be slow-moving and formulaic in what they offer.

The context

OakNorth was a rare new bank in the U.K. when it launched in 2015 to help scale up growing companies with bank funding.

Co-founders Khosla and Joel Perlman met as graduate students at London School of Economics, and started a separate financial analytics business that they later sold. They were surprised by how hard they found it to get bank credit, and saw a gap in the banking market for the "missing middle" of companies too small for commercial loans but past the early startup phase. SoftBank's Vision Fund invested in 2019, and Affinity Partners acquired a stake in 2024.

Khosla has said he wanted to be an entrepreneur since he was around 9 years old, and cut his teeth making investments for the Mittal steel family. Perlman hails from a family of entrepreneurs — one of his brothers helped make a global brand out of Zumba dance classes.

Write to Margot Patrick at margot.patrick@wsj.com

data.title: Germany Producer Prices Rise At Fastest Pace Since 2023
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Germany's producer prices increased at the fastest pace in more than three years in October on rising energy and intermediate goods prices, Destatis said Friday.

Producer prices grew 8.1 percent year-on-year in October, marking the strongest growth since February 2023. Economists had forecast prices to climb 7.2 percent after posting an annual growth of 6.7 percent in September.

On a monthly basis, producer prices gained 1.4 percent compared to economists' forecast of 0.9 percent.

The annual increase in producer prices was primarily due to the 18.7 percent surge in energy prices. The prices of intermediate goods also increased substantially, up by 6.8 percent.

Capital goods prices climbed 2.4 percent and durable consumer goods moved up 2.3 percent from a year earlier. By contrast, lower prices were registered for non-durable consumer goods, which fell 1.3 percent.

When energy prices are excluded, producer prices rose by 3.6 percent from the last year and were up 0.3 percent compared with September.

data.title: Who Would Have Thought a Delicious Drink You Can Chew Could Take a Thai Brand Around the World?
data.description:
BANGKOK, THAILAND, Nov 20, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - A great drink begins with great taste. But when that drink also brings an element of fun to every sip, it becomes something more memorable. This is the idea behind Mogu Mogu, a Thai-born beverage that combines distinctive fruit flavors with generous chunks of chewy nata de coco, creating an experience that can be both sipped and chewed.

Behind the brand is Sappe Public Company Limited (SAPPE), a Thai beverage innovator with a passion for developing delicious and distinctive flavors. Drawing on its expertise in beverage formulation, SAPPE created Mogu Mogu in 2001, pioneering the concept of the Snackable Drink, which the company identifies as the world's first innovation of its kind.

From its beginnings in Thailand, Mogu Mogu has grown into one of SAPPE's flagship brands and played a significant role in the company's international expansion. Today, SAPPE's products reach consumers in more than 100 countries worldwide through over one million points of sale.

Great Taste Comes First, with a Playful Twist

At the heart of Mogu Mogu is SAPPE's expertise in creating beverages with delicious, distinctive, and memorable flavors. This has long been one of the company's key strengths in product innovation.

SAPPE places strong emphasis on developing unique formulations and flavor profiles that stand out from the very first taste. This expertise has enabled Mogu Mogu to offer a diverse range of fruit flavors, each with its own distinctive character.

But SAPPE wanted to create more than a delicious drink. It saw an opportunity to introduce an entirely new experience by incorporating generous chunks of nata de coco into the beverage.

The result was a combination of delicious fruit flavors and a satisfying chewy texture, bringing refreshment and enjoyment together in a single bottle. This distinctive experience became the defining characteristic that sets Mogu Mogu apart from conventional beverages.

Even the name Mogu Mogu evokes the playful experience of chewing, reflecting the enjoyment the brand aims to deliver.

When Great Taste and Fun Cross Borders

Creating a delicious and distinctive beverage is only the beginning. Encouraging consumers from different countries to try something unfamiliar and choose it again is one of the greatest challenges in building a global brand.

For Mogu Mogu, its distinctive flavors, combined with the playful and unexpected experience of chewing, have become powerful strengths. Consumers can discover what makes the product different from their very first sip.

Originating in Thailand, Mogu Mogu expanded into international markets and became one of SAPPE's key brands. The company continues to develop flavors and products that respond to different consumer preferences across markets while working closely with business partners to expand distribution.

Mogu Mogu's journey reflects the philosophy of SAPPE, which began as a small beverage company in Thailand but believed from the outset that innovation was the key to differentiation and competitive opportunity.

Rather than following existing conventions, SAPPE set out to create something genuinely new, focusing on the value it could deliver to consumers through exceptional taste and distinctive drinking experiences. This commitment helped transform a Thai innovation into a recognizable brand in international markets.

More Than a Chewy Drink, a Brand Built on Experience

More than two decades after its launch, Mogu Mogu continues to maintain its distinctive identity by combining delicious fruit flavors with the playful experience of chewing generous chunks of nata de coco. The brand also continues to develop new products and flavors in response to evolving consumer preferences.

For SAPPE, the story of Mogu Mogu demonstrates that successful innovation is not driven by novelty alone. It begins with quality and great taste that consumers genuinely enjoy, combined with creativity that delivers a differentiated experience.

The novelty of a drink you can chew may inspire consumers to try Mogu Mogu for the first time. But it is the memorable taste that gives them a reason to come back for more.

About SAPPE

Sappe Public Company Limited (SAPPE) is a leading Thai beverage innovator and the creator of the world's first Snackable Drink through its iconic global brand, Mogu Mogu. With products reaching consumers in over 100 countries across Asia, Europe, the Middle East, and beyond, SAPPE is committed to creating innovative beverages that respond to evolving consumer lifestyles.

SAPPE's diverse portfolio includes Mogu Mogu, the pioneering fruit juice drink with chewy nata de coco; Sappe Aloe Vera, a refreshing fruit juice drink featuring large aloe vera pieces; and Sappe Beauti, a functional beverage line focused on health and wellness.

Headquartered in Bangkok and listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET: SAPPE), the company is driven by innovation, deep consumer insights, and a commitment to sustainability. Guided by its mission, "We better people's lives through our innovative spirit," SAPPE continues to bring distinctive beverage experiences to consumers worldwide.
